summary: A ring chart that splits one total into parts, such as the hours an agent spent on each kind of task. The total sits in the middle, and a legend beside the ring lists each part with its value and share. Hovering a slice or its legend row highlights both and puts that part's value in the middle.
use: When you want to show where an agent's time, cost or effort went.
When a total breaks into a handful of categories and their shares matter.
When a small dashboard card needs both the total and the breakdown.
features: Draws one arc per entry in `segments`, sized by its share of the total, sweeping in one after another.
The middle shows the total, counting up, with `label` under it; while a part is highlighted it shows that part's value and label instead.
Each legend row shows the value with `unit` and its rounded percent of the total.
Hovering a slice or a row highlights both; `active` and `onActiveChange` let you drive the highlight from outside.
Colours come from the chart palette in order, or from each segment's `color`, and `format` sets how values read (one decimal by default).
a11y: The ring's SVG is aria-hidden, so the values are read from the legend rows as text.
The count-up of the total finishes at once when the user prefers reduced motion.

faq.q: How do I grey out an "Other" slice?
faq.a: Give that segment its own `color`, like 'var(--dm-faint)'. Segments without a color take the next palette colour.

faq.q: Can I highlight a slice from somewhere else on the page?
faq.a: Yes. Pass `active` with the segment's index (or null for none) and update it from your own state; `onActiveChange` tells you when hovering changes it.

faq.q: How do I show money or percentages instead of hours?
faq.a: Pass `format` to write each value and `unit` for the text after it. Both apply to the middle and to every legend row.
